questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being a French citizen without ever have lived in France, I felt the urge to experience a daily life in the French culture. Paris being a crucial european capital with such diversity in its different neighbourhoods was obvious for a semester abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Paris is wonderful, enjoyed the heck out of my daily life. Sorbonne is mesmerizing with its tradition and history, but the teaching method didn't correspond with the way I get the most out of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The updated course catalogue arrived a few months before, and the final course selection was first available the week before. However, didn't have any issue with changing my pre-approval and they are very large with students switching courses within the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't receive any mails until I reached out myself. But when reaching out, they were helpful and quick to respond. We had 2 information meetings in the week before where most was covered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Be aware that you have to be physically present when registrating your courses.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It's a proces where you have to be patient. Our two housings came within the final month before going. Most platforms require a 'Dossier' with documents from both yourself and a cautioner. Use the government authorized 'Dossier Facile' to easily create your Dossier. 
Sorbonne collaborates with different housing platforms, who then prioritizes students attending Sorbonne. We found housing through 'studapart'.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have the opportunity to live within Paris, and not only with other students. I prioritized this as I wished to feel the Parisian vibe rather than Campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sorbonne had its own housing and there's plenty of information, however I didn't apply due to the location.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had a lot of doubt due to the course catalogue not being updated until a few months before. Leave some time the week before to select your courses, there everything will be updated and clear.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to be physically present and fill out a form on paper. The courses are then first come first served, so expect changes in your preferred courses and have some back-ups.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Quick responses on their e-mail and two information meetings the week before, with plenty of opportunity to ask questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what I wanted, however after the first week I changed half of my courses as they didn't match my expectations. This was no problem and went smoothly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and have multiple courses you wish to attend. Show up on time when registrating your courses so you avoid the queue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of different classes, however didn't quite match what I study at home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Most exams are written by hand in class with a French dictionary as you're only aid. 
You have to be comfortable in French to follow along. Further than that make sure that you have an understanding of France's history and culture, as these are the main references used. The courses on English were easier than the ones in French, due to a general lower level of English in France.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Sorbonne it was mostly monologue-based compared to the dialogue-based style at UCPH. Also, the teacher is right and as a student you have to understand their understandings. Not the other way around.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Litterature and politics
Rhetoric and argumentation
Translation from French to English
Language and litterature (English)
American culture and litterature (English)
American cinema (English)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed 'Litterature and politics' as it gave me the most fond understanding of the French academic tradition. We read Victor Hugo and André Malraux.

questions.answer: Less: Dining out and litterature

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't use it as spots for sports filled up too quick

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty of stuff, didn't use it though

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Running ! The Seine (northern side) offers long runs without traffic lights
Read outside - in parks, on a bench or in a café. 
Talk with strangers - Paris is the best place for a small talk before never seeing each other again; enjoy the human energy !

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many museums are free for under 26

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Going from one capital to another (where language wasn't a barrier) felt very comfortable and easy to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go up and ask for help - they are very friendly. I didn't socialize too much with local students as they were also quite younger (French go directly to university)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not leaving much space for students to academically reflect by themselves

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Everybody being outside - in cafés, for an apéritif, dining out or running. 
Talking with strangers - so many lovely encounters over an espresso, whilst running or a glass of wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go out and experience the atmosphere of the city. 
Speak French - even if you're more comfortable in English. 
Bring a book everywhere you go, Paris is a city where everyone's reading.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare for a lot of analogue experiences (I enjoyed it!), be patient with Sorbonne - it will get sorted out, follow the instructions of the teacher on the exams...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living within the French language, culture and tradition for 5 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting and accepting the style of teaching.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
